'Reveal the top card of your deck. Prevent the next X arcane damage that would be dealt to your hero this turn, where X is 4 minus the pitch value of the card revealed this way.'

REVEAL_TOP_DECK (handler effect_types.py ~2229 reads amount/into) reveals the top card public and stores it as a list under ref 'revealed'; an empty deck stores []. REF_PITCH_IS unwraps a single-element list and tests pitch 1/2/3 = red/yellow/blue (condition_types.py ~1979).

WHY NESTED CONDITIONALS FOR X: _resolve_amount (effect_types.py ~18-217) has arithmetic (SUM/X plus-minus) over ROLL/COUNT/event expressions but NO expression for 'pitch value of a referenced card', so '4 - pitch' cannot be computed inline - an invented token would silently resolve to 0. The four cases are branched exactly: no card revealed -> REF_EXISTS False -> else -> prevent 4 (release note 3); pitch 1/2/3 -> prevent 3/2/1.

PREVENT_DAMAGE (handler effect_types.py ~5254 reads amount - expression-capable but given literals here - damage_type, source_class) registers a one-shot PREVENTION replacement on my hero for arcane damage only.

Two approximations inherent to the shared primitive, stated not hidden: (a) 'this turn' - ReplacementEffect has no lifespan (effects.py ~121-147), so if no arcane damage arrives this turn the shield persists into later turns instead of expiring; (b) 'the next X arcane damage' across MULTIPLE events - the replacement reduces the first qualifying event by up to N and is then consumed, whereas the printed text would spread the prevention across successive events this turn. A single damage event larger than X behaves correctly (reduced to 0... to within X). Fixing either needs generic replacement-expiry/partial-consumption work in effects.py, not card JSON.
